 View Comments After a season-opening loss, Joe Mazzulla has the Celtics rolling. Barry Chin/Globe Staff Can the Celtics keep their luck rolling? 
 The Celtics overcame a poor shooting performance from behind the arc to claim a 108-97 road win over the Magic Sunday. Boston missed 32 of 44 3-pointers, yet remained committed to a stingy defensive approach. 
 “Our defensive intensity didn’t wane, and our poise to continue to get great shots didn’t wane,” Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla said. “We have to be able to do that on both ends. We have to be able to trust the next possession and play through and continue to generate great shots, which we did. Our defense, even when we gave up some offensive rebounds, we stayed connected. 
 “That’s the mindset of the team.” 
 In the second night of a back-to-back on the road, the Celtics will need to rely on that same mindset to best the Rockets. 
 Paul George has been key to that defensive identity. He posted 17 points, six rebounds, eight assists, two steals, and two blocks against the Magic.

Enter Email Sign Up The 36-year-old George has long been renowned for his ability to contribute on both ends of the court, a skill set that made him an attractive target for the Celtics. 
 “We continue to get better,” said Jayson Tatum, who scored 32 points and added seven assists. “His awareness on the defensive end and his activity with his hands is next level. He just always has awareness for the ball, deflections, and he makes it easy for the rest of us, even this late in his career.”

 When: Monday, 8:30 p.m. 
 Where: Toyota Center, Houston 
 TV: NBCSB. Radio: WBZ-FM 98.5. 
 Line: Houston -5. O/U: 218.5. 
 CELTICS 
 Season record: 5-1. vs. spread: 3-2, 1 push. Over/under: 3-2, 1 push 
 Last 10 games: 6-4. vs. spread: 4-5, 1 push. Over/under: 5-4, 1 push 
 ROCKETS 
 Season record: 6-1. vs. spread: 6-1. Over/under: 5-2 
 Last 10 games: 8-2. vs. spread: 8-2. Over/under: 6-4 
 TEAM STATISTICS 
 Points per game: Boston 118.7, Houston 120.7 
 Points allowed per game: Boston 109.2, Houston 108.3 
 Field goal percentage: Boston .469, Houston .492 
 Opponent field goal percentage: Boston .427, Houston .455 
 3-point percentage: Boston .355, Houston .390 
 Opponent 3-point percentage: Boston .338, Houston .301 
 Stat of the day: The Rockets have won three straight games at home. 
 Notes: In order to keep Fred VanVleet from playing both games of back-to-backs, the Rockets signed Marcus Smart — an old friend of the Celtics. Smart got his first start of the season and scored 24 points in a 119-98 win over the Thunder Saturday. ... “It’s the reason he’s here and the reason we made him a target of ours,” Rockets coach Ime Udoka said of Smart. “If any injury goes down, you can easily plug him into the lineup. He’s a very competent starter, a guy that started most of his career but has also come off the bench and is just as effective.” ... Mitchell Robinson is listed as out for the Celtics, who cited rest.
